name: All for One and One for All Poker
description: All for One and One for All is a high-churn variant of Five-Card Draw. Unlike standard poker where you draw once, here players can repeatedly exchange their entire hand or a single card through multiple rounds of betting until the deck is nearly exhausted.

overview.description: All for One and One for All is a high-churn variant of Five-Card Draw. Unlike standard poker where you draw once, here players can repeatedly exchange their entire hand or a single card through multiple rounds of betting until the deck is nearly exhausted.

history.origins: A relatively modern home-game variant of Five-Card Draw. Its name is a playful reference to the Three Musketeers, echoing the 'One card or All cards' binary choice of the discard phase.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Appears in American 'dealer's choice' home games.
1990s-2000s: Described in printed home-game rules and early online poker variant archives.
history.cultural: Popular in low-stakes social poker nights where 'active' games with lots of betting rounds are preferred.
history.evolution: Evolved from standard Draw Poker by removing the one-draw limit, turning the game into one of attrition and probability tracking.

setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards face-down. Antes are placed.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best 5-card poker hand at showdown or by forcing all other players to fold.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Initial Deal**: 5 cards each. Initial betting round. 2. **Repeated Draw Phases**: Each active player must choose one of three options: 
   - **All for One**: Discard your entire 5-card hand and draw 5 new ones.
   - **One for All**: Discard exactly 1 card and draw 1 new one.
   - **Stand Pat**: Keep your current hand (once you stand pat, you cannot draw in future rounds).
3. **Betting**: Each draw phase is followed by a full betting round. 4. **Repetition**: Draw and betting rounds continue until the deck has too few cards left to fulfill a worst-case draw scenario (i.e., every participant drawing 5). 5. **Showdown**: Remaining players reveal hands. Best hand according to standard rankings wins.
keyRules: No half-measures: You cannot discard 2, 3, or 4 cards. It is strictly 1 or 5 or 0.
Standing Pat: Once a player stands pat, they are locked into that hand for the remainder of the deal.
End Condition: The game ends automatically when the deck contains fewer than (Active Players * 5) cards, or by mutual agreement if betting becomes circular.

strategy.basic: If you don't have at least a pair, go 'All for One'. If you have a potential flush/straight draw, go 'One for All'.
strategy.intermediate: Bluffing: Standing pat early can scare opponents into thinking you have a made hand, even if you are holding junk. However, they have many rounds to figure you out.
strategy.advanced: Card Counting: Because so many cards are being cycled (draw 5, draw 5...), you can track which cards are unlikely to appear in and your opponents' hands. If many Spades have been discarded, your flush draw is dead.
tips: The deck disappears fast. If 6 people are playing and 4 draw 'All for One', the deck is half gone in one round.
Don't be afraid to 'All for One' twice in a row if your first exchange is also rubbish.

variations.name: Musketeer Wilds
variations.description: Deuces/Jacks are wild to increase the power level of the multiple draws.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation adjusts wild cards only; engine-level parameter overrides for wilds are not yet modeled.

scoring.description: Pot game scored by standard high-hand poker ranking at showdown.

synthesis.shortDescription: A thrilling high-attrition Poker variant. Burn through the deck as you repeatedly swap either one card or your entire hand in a race for the perfect showdown.
